case_id_security.key_reproducibility: IDs are intentionally unstable between evaluator processes; stable oracle targets committed without IDs
case_id_security.scheme: HMAC-SHA256, 128-bit truncated ID, 256-bit ephemeral evaluator-only key
case_id_security.scope: Participant sandbox only; not source confidentiality outside sandbox or prevention of replay from published observed fixtures

checkpoints: none; benchmark definition and CPU baselines only; existing champion preserved
known_failures: This is a published deterministic synthetic regression benchmark. A solver can precompute truths or reconstruct law families from public observations and source; HMAC IDs do not make these cases scientifically novel.
Only untrusted code actually launched via sandbox_evaluator.py is segregated from oracle.py; direct import/grade calls inside the host interpreter are explicitly trusted, not sealed.
Bubblewrap relies on Linux namespace support and kernel security; not a proof of sandbox escape resistance or multi-tenant host isolation.
Ephemeral HMAC IDs are not cross-process reproducible. Numeric fixtures, counts and commitments excluding IDs are reproducible; exact hidden-run replay requires a secure external evaluator/key.
A short prefix can admit high-degree interpolation; matching a private label is not a formal invariant or evidence of learning/generalization.
No fresh secret-seed adversarial holdout, authenticated independent reviewer approval, champion modification, training, GPU or network use.
oracle_target_commitment_method: SHA256 of compact sorted-key JSON array of reference_exact entries in canonical generator order, EXCLUDING ephemeral case IDs; fixture integrity only, not confidentiality
proof_scope: 99 published CPU fixture cases (12 families) and capped namespace-isolated participant execution. The original 99/99 public-ID inversion and 9/9 ID-only periodic replay no longer work; old finite fixture remains learnable/memorizable from its observations. This is not a cryptographic hidden challenge set, a formal theorem, or a learned discovery result.

rework_of_review.finding: Public SHA256(seed,family,split,rep) case_id inverted in 99/99; ID-only periodic future/law exploit passed 9/9
rework_of_review.fix: HMAC per evaluator process; sandbox excludes oracle, secret, workspace and network; independent negative tests block published ID inversion and source import
rework_of_review.remaining_limit: Open fixed-seed fixture can be reconstructed by a source-aware solver from observed prefix; no unseen-seed or hidden-family novelty claim

runtime_dependencies: Linux bubblewrap (bwrap) executable for isolated candidate evaluation
Linux user, mount, PID, IPC and network namespaces

sandbox.linux_isolation: bubblewrap --unshare-all --clearenv, read-only /usr /lib /lib64 and candidate.py, no oracle mount
sandbox.protocol: public encoded JSONL stdin -> JSONL (case_id,forecast,law) stdout
sandbox.resource_caps: 5s CPU, 15s wall, 512MiB address space, 1MiB output, 64KiB candidate source

title: Construct falsifiable invariant-discovery benchmark across dynamical families

verification_targets.family_generation: recompute oracle cases and exact/Decimal reference values from committed sources
verification_targets.fixed_numeric_fixture: Recompute 99 cases and stable report hashes regardless of fresh HMAC ID key
verification_targets.heldout_separation: check public views omit truth/family/params; verify no future samples read by baselines
